LAYER_SPECS.name: swc
LAYER_SPECS.description: Software components, one file each under `swc/{group}/`; the group is the file's directory, not a key inside the file.

LAYER_SPECS.name: interfaces
LAYER_SPECS.description: Port interfaces. Three element kinds discriminated by `kind`: `sender_receiver` (typed data elements), `client_server` (operations with typed, directional arguments) and `external_interface` (a stub for an interface declared outside the project, carrying the reference the source made to it).

LAYER_SPECS.name: connectors
LAYER_SPECS.description: Assembly connectors, each joining one component's `provide` port to another component's `require` port over a compatible interface.

LAYER_SPECS.name: implementation_types
LAYER_SPECS.description: Implementation data types, one file each under `data_types/implementation/`: how the platform stores the data a model exchanges. Six element kinds discriminated by `kind` (`value_type`, `reference_type`, `external_type`, `implementation_record`, `implementation_array`, `pointer`), plus one nested member kind (`implementation_element`). A `value_type` is the implementation type that rests on a base type, an element of the `base_types` layer, a `reference_type` rests on another implementation type, and `implementation_record`, `implementation_array` and `pointer` are the implementation structure, array and pointer; a mapping set pairs each application type, an element of the `application_types` layer, with the implementation type that stores it. An `external_type` is a stub for an implementation type declared outside the project. An implementation type and an application type may carry one name. The directory is mandatory and may be empty.

LAYER_SPECS.name: requirements
LAYER_SPECS.description: Requirements and specification items, identified by `id` rather than `name`; the architecture elements that realize one name it in their own `satisfies`. An architecture requirement is published in the generated `needs.json` as a need of its own; an imported one is never published, only named by its id in the links that reach it.

LAYER_SPECS.name: systems
LAYER_SPECS.description: Top-level systems of the architecture layer.

LAYER_SPECS.name: containers
LAYER_SPECS.description: Containers, each referencing the system it belongs to.

LAYER_SPECS.name: tasks
LAYER_SPECS.description: OS tasks and the runnables each one executes. `period` is in seconds; a budget, `wcet`, carries its own unit.

LAYER_SPECS.name: sequences
LAYER_SPECS.description: Sequence scenarios, one task each; each is drawn as a sequence diagram whose files are named from the scenario's name.

LAYER_SPECS.name: resources
LAYER_SPECS.description: The one optional layer, and the only one whose checks a project turns on by having it: where it is present, every `Task.core` must resolve to a `cpu_core`, and every SWC is a consumer of every declared memory pool.
LAYER_SPECS.absent_description: The one optional layer, ABSENT in this project — so no resource rule runs at all. Its inventory is a registry fact rather than project state, so it is published in full: a client can author the first `cpu_core` or `memory` budget without a second round trip, and the `create` materializes the directory as a registry-internal side effect (ADR 011 decision 1).

PLACEMENT_FIELDS.name: group
PLACEMENT_FIELDS.description: Placement metadata: the value is the element's directory rather than a key in its file. Validated as a single path segment, never as an AUTOSAR identifier, and immutable — nothing moves an element between groups, so a change of group is a remove and a create.

KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.swc: One software component: its ports, its runnable entities, the inter-runnable variables those runnables share and the exclusive areas that keep them from preempting each other.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.port: One port of a software component: a named, directed endpoint typed by an interface. A `provide` port offers the interface, a `require` port consumes it, and an assembly connector joins one of each. A port of an external stub carries its name and direction only: the source states no interface for it. `kind:compositions.composition_port` declares the same four fields for a composition's boundary port; the two are duplicated rather than shared because a bare kind name is unique across the whole contract and `memberOf` is derived per layer.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.runnable: One runnable entity of a software component: a schedulable function with its timing constraint, the events that trigger it — periodic, at start-up, a client's call of an operation the component provides, the reception of a data element on one of its require ports, or the return of an asynchronous call of its component — whether it may be started again while it runs, the C symbol its entry point is generated under, and the data it touches through the component's own ports — the data elements it `reads` and `writes`, explicitly or implicitly, and the operations it `calls`, synchronously or asynchronously, each entry naming a port and a member of that port's interface — the variables of its own component it reads and writes without a port, in `reads_variables` and `writes_variables`, and the exclusive areas of its own component it enters by API, in `can_enter`, or runs inside as a whole, in `runs_inside`. A runnable is mapped to an OS task through the task's `runnables` list, by its component — the type by `swc` or the occurrence by `instance` — and the runnable's `name`, and the runnable of one occurrence to at most one task.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.timing_event: A periodic trigger: the runnable is invoked every `period` seconds, except in the modes `disabled_modes` names. Every field is part of the event's identity, so a changed period is one event removed and another added, never an edit in place; a field still at its default is left out of the identity, so an event that disables no mode is addressed by its `type` and `period` alone.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.init_event: An initialization event: the runnable runs once at start-up. It carries its `type` and, when stated, its `name`, so a runnable either has it or does not.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.sender_receiver: A sender-receiver interface: the set of typed data elements exchanged over a port. Discriminated from `client_server` by `kind: sender_receiver`; it must declare at least one data element.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.client_server: A client-server interface: the set of operations a server port offers and a client port calls, each with its typed, directional arguments. Discriminated by `kind: client_server`; it must declare at least one operation.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.data_element: One data element of a sender-receiver interface: a name, the declared data type it carries (`application_type` for an application data type, `implementation_type` for an implementation data type), an optional `init` value it starts from, and an optional `asil` for the safety integrity level of the information it carries.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.operation: One operation of a client-server interface: a name and its ordered, typed, directional arguments; an operation may take no arguments at all.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.argument: One argument of a client-server operation: its name, the direction data flows through it, and the declared data type it carries (`application_type` for an application data type, `implementation_type` for an implementation data type).
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.connector: One assembly connector: it links the `from` endpoint, which must be a `provide` port, to the `to` endpoint, which must be a `require` port, and the `to` port's interface must be satisfied by the `from` port's. Connector names are unique across the layer, and so is each `(from, to)` link.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.connector_endpoint: One end of an assembly connector: the component or composition type that owns the port, and the port. A nested object rather than a list member, so it has no identity of its own and every field of it may change. It names the TYPE either way; the writer resolves that type to the member of it inside the connector's own composition, which is why a type may stand only once per composition.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.enum: An enumeration type: a set of named values, each with an integer value. Emitted as an `APPLICATION-PRIMITIVE-DATA-TYPE` of category `VALUE`. Its values are stated in one of two forms: inline as `literals`, from which a `{name}_CompuMethod` of category `TEXTTABLE` is generated that maps each literal to its value, or by `compu_method_ref`, naming a `texttable` element of the `compu_methods` layer, which generates no form.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.record: A record (structure) type: an ordered list of named, typed fields. Field names are unique inside the record, and a field's type must name a declared data type that does not, directly or through other records and arrays, contain this record again.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.array: A fixed-length array type: `length` elements of one declared `element_type`. The element type must name a declared data type and must not close a cycle back to this array.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.enum_literal: One named value of an `enum` type: a member of its `literals` collection, never a standalone element, so it has no file and no layer-level address.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.record_field: A member of a `record` type's `fields` collection; like `enum_literal` it has no file and no layer-level address.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.value_type: An implementation data type of category `VALUE`, emitted as an `IMPLEMENTATION-DATA-TYPE` whose `BASE-TYPE-REF` points at its `base`, which must name a declared base type. It is what a data element or an argument names as its type, and what a mapping set pairs with the application type it stores; a record field and an array element name the application view instead. A declared `value_min` or `value_max` is written as the type's own `{name}_Range` `DATA-CONSTR`, one rule of `INTERNAL-CONSTRS` with each declared bound as a `CLOSED` limit, referenced by a `DATA-CONSTR-REF`; `unit` reaches no ARXML element.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.base_type: A base type: how the platform stores a value — its size in bits, its encoding and its C declaration — emitted as a `SW-BASE-TYPE`. A base type is never what a data prototype is typed by (AUTOSAR's `AutosarDataPrototype.type`): no data element, argument, record field or array element may name one. A base type is an element of its own layer, `base_types`, so it may share its name with a type of another layer. A `value_type` names it as its `base`, and the data prototypes name the `value_type`.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.requirement: One requirement or specification item. Identified by `id` rather than `name`, and its file is named from the `id`; the elements that realize it name it in their `satisfies` as `<id>@<version>`, so the requirement file names no element and an imported one can be overwritten by a re-import without losing a link, or removed by one when the delivery no longer holds it. `document`, `baseline` and `revision` record where an external requirement came from. An architecture requirement is published in the generated `needs.json` as a need of its own; an imported one is never published, only named by its id in the links that reach it.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.system: One top-level system of the architecture view: a C4 context-level element that names a boundary of the architecture. It is what the landscape view draws when this layer is populated, and it reaches the LikeC4 model and no ARXML element.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.container: One container of the architecture view: a C4 container-level element that belongs to exactly one declared system. It reaches the LikeC4 model and no ARXML element.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.task: One OS task: a periodic schedulable unit with a priority, a partition assignment, an optional worst-case execution budget and the ordered list of runnables it executes. A task's period must be a divisor of every timing period among the runnables it maps.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.task_runnable_ref: One entry of a task's `runnables` list: a runnable of a software component, the component named by exactly one of `swc` (a component type placed at most once below the root composition, or not at all) and `instance` (one occurrence of a component below the root composition). The `(swc, instance, runnable)` triple, the absent selector as `null`, is the member's identity, because runnable names are unique only inside their own component.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.sequence: One sequence scenario: an ordered walk through some of the runnables of exactly one task, drawn as a sequence diagram. The steps must follow the task's own runnable order.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.sequence_step: One step of a sequence scenario: the runnable it shows, its component named by exactly one of `swc` and `instance`, with an optional note. The `(swc, instance, runnable)` triple, the absent selector as `null`, is the step's identity; the step must be mapped to the scenario's task, and a step written the same way appears at most once per scenario.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.cpu_core: A CPU-load budget for one core, referenced from `Task.core` by its `core` number. Once any `cpu_core` resource exists, every task's core must have one; `advisory` enforcement is the per-resource opt-out.
KIND_DESCRIPTIONS.memory: A memory-pool budget, referenced by the keys of `SWComponent.memory`. Every software component is a consumer of every declared pool: under `strict` enforcement each must declare a budget for it, under `advisory` a missing budget counts as zero and a breach is reported as information.

FIELD_ANNOTATIONS.description: The component's identity; the file is named from it (`swc/{group}/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across all software components, must not be empty, and immutable — renaming is a remove and a create.
The AUTOSAR component category. Only `application` is emitted today — the ARXML writer refuses a `service` or `ecu_abstraction` component — so the default is the one value that generates.

Free text about the component, shown on the component's box in the diagrams when non-empty, and written into the generated ARXML as the component type's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none. An external component emits no element, so its text reaches the diagrams only.

The component's ports, addressed by `name`, which must be unique inside the component. Each port is typed by a declared interface and joined to another component by an assembly connector; an external stub's port declares no interface.

The component's runnable entities, addressed by `name`, which must be unique inside the component — and only there, which is why a task or a sequence names a runnable by its component — the type by `swc` or the occurrence by `instance` — and the runnable's `name`.

Memory-pool budgets, in bytes, keyed by the name of a declared `memory` resource. Checked by the resource analysis once the project declares any resource; `resources/` is an optional layer, and in a project without one an unknown key is reported by no check.
The port's identity inside its component; unique among the component's ports and immutable.
Whether the port offers the interface (`provide`) or consumes it (`require`). An assembly connector runs from a `provide` port to a `require` port, never between two of the same direction.

The name of the declared interface this port is typed by. The two ends of a connector need not name the same interface: the required port's interface must be satisfied by the provided port's. Absent on an external stub's port, which never carries one; a port of any other component without one is reported.
Free text about the port. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.
The runnable's identity inside its component; unique among the component's runnables and immutable. It is prefixed `TMT_` and `IT_` for the generated event names.
The minimum interval, in seconds, between two starts of the runnable (0 means no minimum). Must be >= 0; neither this field nor any other float accepts NaN or ±Infinity.

The events that trigger the runnable: periodic `timing` events, the start-up `init` event, `operation` events, each naming an operation a client calls through one of the component's own `provide` ports, `data` events, each naming a data element whose reception through one of the component's own `require` ports starts it, and `call_returned` events, each naming an operation a runnable of the component calls asynchronously, whose return starts it and whose result it fetches. A union-typed collection whose members carry no identity field: a member IS its value, so a changed period, port, operation or element is one event removed and one added.
The discriminator of a timing event; always `timing`.
The period of the trigger, in seconds. Must be > 0.
The discriminator of an initialization event; always `init`.

The interface's identity; the file is named from it (`interfaces/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across every interface kind, must not be blank, and immutable.
The discriminator that selects this interface kind; always `sender_receiver`.
The typed data elements exchanged over the interface, addressed by `name`, which must be unique inside the interface. Must not be empty.
Free text about the interface. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

The interface's identity; the file is named from it (`interfaces/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across every interface kind, must not be blank, and immutable.
The discriminator that selects this interface kind; always `client_server`.
The operations a server port offers and a client port calls, addressed by `name`, which must be unique inside the interface. Must not be empty.
Free text about the interface. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.
The data element's identity inside its interface; unique among the interface's data elements and immutable.

The name of the declared implementation data type this data element carries, an element of the `implementation_types` layer: a value type, a reference type, an implementation record, an implementation array, a pointer or an external data type stub. Exactly one of `application_type` and `implementation_type` is set.

The value this data element starts from, where the design fixes one. Optional, and its shape follows the element's own declared type: a plain scalar for an application type, for a value type or for a reference type (judged against the type at the end of its chain), the literal's own name for an enumeration, the name of one of the table's entries for a value type or a reference type that references a table (itself or along its chain), a map keyed by exactly the declared field or element names for a record or an implementation record, and a list of exactly the declared length for an array or an implementation array. A pointer takes none. A value the declared type cannot hold is reported as a model error rather than converted. A port of a component may state a value of its own for the element in its `com_specs`, which takes precedence on that port.
The operation's identity inside its interface; unique among the interface's operations and immutable.
The operation's ordered arguments, addressed by `name`, which must be unique inside the operation. May be empty.
The argument's identity inside its operation; unique among the operation's arguments and immutable.
The direction data flows through the argument: `in` from client to server, `out` from server to client, `inout` both ways.

The name of the declared implementation data type this argument carries, an element of the `implementation_types` layer: a value type, a reference type, an implementation record, an implementation array, a pointer or an external data type stub. Exactly one of `application_type` and `implementation_type` is set.

The connector's identity; the file is named from it (`connectors/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the layer, must not be empty, and immutable.
The providing endpoint: the component and the `provide` port the connector starts from. Its port's interface must satisfy the `to` port's, which the same interface always does.
The requiring endpoint: the component and the `require` port the connector delivers to. Its port's interface must be satisfied by the `from` port's, which the same interface always does.
Free text about the connector. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.
The name of the declared software component that owns the endpoint's port. Exactly one of `swc` and `composition` is set; this one is the endpoint of an ordinary component.
The name of a port of that component. Must not be empty; the port's existence and its direction are checked against the component.

The type's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/application/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the application types, must not be blank, and immutable; an implementation type may carry the same name. Where the enumeration states `literals`, it is suffixed `_CompuMethod` for the generated computation method.
The discriminator that selects this data type kind; always `enum`.

The enumeration's named literals, addressed by `name`: the inline form of its values, from which the `{name}_CompuMethod` is generated. Absent where the enumeration names a `texttable` by its `compu_method_ref` instead; it states exactly one of the two, and stated literals must not be empty.
Free text about the type. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

The type's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/application/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the application types, must not be blank, and immutable; an implementation type may carry the same name.
The discriminator that selects this data type kind; always `record`.
The record's named, typed fields in declaration order, addressed by `name`. Must not be empty.
Free text about the type. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

The type's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/application/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the application types, must not be blank, and immutable; an implementation type may carry the same name.
The discriminator that selects this data type kind; always `array`.

The name of the declared data type of every element: an application type, an enumeration, a record or an array, an element of the `application_types` layer — a composite's members are typed by the physical view. It may not be this array itself, nor a type that contains this array.
The number of elements in the array. Must be > 0.
Free text about the type. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.
The literal's identity inside its enumeration; unique among the enumeration's literals and immutable.
The integer the literal stands for. Unique among the enumeration's literals; emitted as the literal's `LOWER-LIMIT`/`UPPER-LIMIT` in the computation method.
The field's identity inside its record; unique among the record's fields and immutable.

The name of the declared data type the field carries: an application type, an enumeration, a record or an array, an element of the `application_types` layer — a composite's members are typed by the physical view. It may not close a cycle back to the record.

The type's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/implementation/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the implementation types, must not be blank, and immutable; an application type may carry the same name.
The discriminator that selects this data type kind; always `value_type`.
Must name a declared base type, an element of the `base_types` layer. A base type is resolved in that layer alone, so it may carry the value type's own name.

The physical unit of the value, as free text (for example `km/h`). Documentation only; it reaches no ARXML element: Table 5.18 of the software component template gives an implementation data type's `unit` no place in any category, and `[constr_1009]` makes the table binding.
The lower bound of the value; omitted or `null` when there is none. Must be <= `value_max` when both are given; neither accepts NaN or ±Infinity.
The upper bound of the value; omitted or `null` when there is none. Must be >= `value_min` when both are given; neither accepts NaN or ±Infinity.
Free text about the type. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

The type's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/base/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the base types, must not be blank, and immutable.

Always `base_type`. The layer holds one kind and is not discriminated; the field is an ordinary literal, kept, immutable as it was, so a base type file reads as it did when base types were a kind of the data types layer.
The size of the base type, in bits. Must be > 0.
A required AUTOSAR BASE-TYPE-ENCODING token (NONE, 2C, IEEE754, ...); must not be blank, because a blank one is not round-trippable through the ARXML importer.

The C type name the generated code declares for this base type (for example `uint8_t`), emitted exactly as written as its `NATIVE-DECLARATION`. Required by check-model: SWCraft never derives one, so a base type without it still loads, but check-model reports it and ARXML generation refuses it until it is filled in.
Free text about the type. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

The requirement's identity; the file is named from it (`requirements/{id}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the layer, must not be empty, and immutable. It is the need's id in the generated `needs.json`, as written, and the id a link to the requirement names there. It may not contain `@` or `:`, the separators of a link's version and of an element reference.
The requirement's one-line title; an architecture requirement's published need carries it as its title.
The requirement's statement; an architecture requirement's published need carries it as its content. Required: a requirement without a statement is not one.
`req` for a requirement, `spec` for a specification item; an architecture requirement is published as the need type `arch_req` or `arch_spec`.

The system's identity; the file is named from it (`systems/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the layer, must not be empty, and immutable; it becomes the LikeC4 element name.
The human-readable title shown on the C4 diagram.
Free text about the system, rendered into the LikeC4 diagram when non-empty.
The container's identity and its filename: `containers/{name}.yaml`. Unique across the layer, must not be empty, and immutable; it becomes the LikeC4 element name.
The human-readable title shown on the C4 diagram.
The name of the declared system this container belongs to; a container belongs to exactly one.
Free text about the container, rendered into the LikeC4 diagram when non-empty.

The task's identity; the file is named from it (`tasks/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the layer, must not be empty, and immutable.
The task's activation period, in seconds (a budget, `wcet`, carries its own unit). Must be > 0.
Must be >= 0; higher is more urgent.
Must be >= 0. Once any `cpu_core` resource exists, every task's core must resolve to one.

The task's execution-time budget: what the architect allots to the task, an upper bound the model is checked against and never a measurement. Written as a whole number followed by its unit, one of `ns`, `us`, `ms` or `s` — `1200us`, `2ms` — with no space, no leading zero, no decimal point and at most 18 digits; omitted or `null` when no budget is declared, greater than zero when present, and a `strict` core budget requires one on every task of that core. Analysis input only: the standard's execution-time constraint names an executable entity, and an OS task is none, so no ARXML output carries it. A file still spelling `wcet_us` is refused with the new spelling.
Free text about the task. Carried in the model; it reaches no generated artifact.
The runnables the task executes, in order, each naming its component by exactly one of `swc` and `instance`, and its `runnable`; an entry written the same way appears at most once in a task.
The name of the declared software component that owns the runnable; exactly one of `swc` and `instance` is set. Part of the member's composite identity, and so immutable.
The name of a runnable of that component. Part of the composite identity, and so immutable; a runnable of one resolved component is mapped to at most one task across the model.
The scenario's identity, which also names its sequence diagram's files. Must match ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ — a rule of this layer alone, deliberately not the AUTOSAR `Identifier` rule.
The name of the declared task this scenario walks; exactly one per scenario, and every step must be mapped to it.
The scenario's human-readable title, shown after its name in the heading of its sequence diagram (`sd {name} — {title}`). When empty, the heading is the name alone.
The steps of the scenario, in order. Must not be empty and must be an ordered subsequence of the referenced task's runnables.
The name of the declared software component the step runs in; exactly one of `swc` and `instance` is set. Part of the step's composite identity, and so immutable.
The name of a runnable of that component, which must be mapped to the scenario's task. Part of the composite identity, and so immutable.
Free text shown beside the step on its sequence diagram; when non-empty the step's activation is labelled `{runnable} — {note}`.
The resource's identity and its filename: `resources/{name}.yaml`. Unique across both resource kinds and immutable.
The discriminator that selects this resource kind; always `cpu_core`.
Must be >= 0, and matches `Task.core`. Immutable: a different core is a different budget, not an edit of this one.
A finite fraction in (0, 1]. RAISING it weakens the check, which is a safety act the server classifies from the staged before/after values, whatever the scope says.

How a breach of this budget is reported. `strict` (the default): every task on the core must declare `wcet` and an over-threshold load is an error. `advisory`: a missing budget counts as zero and a breach is an information line.
Free text about the budget. Carried in the model; it reaches no generated artifact.
The resource's identity and its filename: `resources/{name}.yaml`, and the pool name a component's `memory` map keys. Unique across both resource kinds and immutable.
The discriminator that selects this resource kind; always `memory`.
Must be > 0. ENLARGING it weakens the check, so it is a safety act.
The share of the pool the components' budgets may total before the budget is breached: a finite fraction in (0, 1].

How a breach of this budget is reported. `strict` (the default): every component must declare a budget for the pool and an over-threshold total is an error. `advisory`: a missing budget counts as zero and a breach is an information line.
Free text about the budget. Carried in the model; it reaches no generated artifact.
